rows.algorithm: binary-trees with one bump-allocated buffer of u32-index nodes in every language (B9); the sum of every tree check (README.md).

skip.mk-wrap: not needed for the budgets; written if the checked column shows an overflow-check cost

rows.algorithm: fannkuch-redux: every permutation of n, counting prefix reversals; checksum * 1000 + maxflips (README.md).

skip.mk-wrap: not needed for the budgets; written if the checked column shows an overflow-check cost

rows.algorithm: Integers in [-1e9, 1e9] to decimal text with the textbook digit loop, then the byte sum, rounds times (README.md).

skip.mk-wrap: not needed for the budgets; written if the checked column shows an overflow-check cost

rows.algorithm: Sum of n int64 values in 0..1023, repeated rounds times with a write-back between passes (README.md).
A JSON tokenizer over a 32 MB generated document, hashing every token, repeated rounds times (README.md).

skip.mk-wrap: the hash already uses the wrapping operators in every column (overflow class wraps)

rows.algorithm: Scalar Mandelbrot over an n by n grid, at most 50 iterations per point; the checksum is the total iteration count (README.md).

skip.mk-wrap: the hot loop is float; its only integer arithmetic is the iteration counter

rows.algorithm: Five-body leapfrog in f64, structure of arrays, steps of 0.0078125; the checksum is the final energy times 1e9 truncated to an integer (README.md).

skip.mk-wrap: the hot loop has no integer arithmetic beyond loop counters, so a wrapping column would equal mk

rows.algorithm: Spectral norm of the infinite matrix A(i,j) = 1/((i+j)(i+j+1)/2+i+1) by 10 power iterations of AtA (the Benchmarks Game's spectral-norm, scalar) (README.md).

skip.mk-wrap: not needed for the budgets; A(i, j)'s integer arithmetic is checked in mk

rows.algorithm: Dense f64 matrix multiply, i-k-j loop over flat row-major arrays, repeated rounds times into one result; exact by construction (README.md).

skip.mk-wrap: only index arithmetic is integer; a wrapping column is not needed for the budgets

rows.algorithm: Process start, print one line, exit. Reported and never subtracted from another row (B15).
notes: Times of a few milliseconds are below the 1 s floor by nature: this row exists to show the startup cost each other row carries.

rows.algorithm: Sieve of Eratosthenes over n + 1 byte flags, rounds times; the checksum is rounds times the count of primes up to n (README.md).
Go 1.27's pdqsortOrdered written out for int64 in every language, over four patterns of n keys per round (README.md).
